In this hypothetical world, Method 1 is more correct because it isolates the causal effect of eating citrus on scurvy by conditioning on the intermediate variable (vitamin C). Method 2 suffers from confounding bias because the correlation between eating citrus and scurvy in general could be driven by other factors (such as age, diet, or genetics) that also affect vitamin C levels.
